request.user:
[2024 fall ms math-stat — problem 2]

Single observation $Y$ with density $f(y\mid\theta) = (\theta+1)y^\theta$, $0<y<1$. Test $H_0: \theta = 0$ vs $H_a: \theta > 0$ at level $\alpha$. (1) Show a UMP test exists, find it, and give its exact form in terms of $\alpha$. (2) Give its power function in terms of $\alpha$.

response.text:
Let \(Y\) have density

\[
f(y\mid \theta)=(\theta+1)y^\theta,\qquad 0<y<1,
\]

where \(\theta>-1\). We test

\[
H_0:\theta=0 \qquad \text{vs.}\qquad H_a:\theta>0
\]

at level \(\alpha\).

---

## (1) Existence and form of the UMP level \(\alpha\) test

Under \(H_0\), \(\theta=0\), so

\[
f(y\mid 0)=1,\qquad 0<y<1,
\]

and hence

\[
Y\mid \theta=0 \sim \operatorname{Unif}(0,1).
\]

For any fixed \(\theta>0\), the likelihood ratio of \(f(y\mid \theta)\) against \(f(y\mid 0)\) is

\[
\frac{f(y\mid \theta)}{f(y\mid 0)}
= (\theta+1)y^\theta.
\]

Since \(\theta>0\), this likelihood ratio is strictly increasing in \(y\). Therefore, by the Neyman–Pearson lemma, the most powerful level \(\alpha\) test of

\[
H_0:\theta=0
\]

against the simple alternative

\[
H_1:\theta=\theta_1>0
\]

rejects \(H_0\) for large values of \(Y\). The critical value is chosen so that the size is \(\alpha\).

Because under \(H_0\), \(Y\sim \operatorname{Unif}(0,1)\),

\[
P_0(Y>c)=1-c.
\]

We require

\[
1-c=\alpha,
\]

so

\[
c=1-\alpha.
\]

Thus the test is

\[
\phi(Y)=
\begin{cases}
1, & Y>1-\alpha,\\
0, & Y\le 1-\alpha.
\end{cases}
\]

Equivalently, since the distribution is continuous, one may use \(Y\ge 1-\alpha\) without changing the size.

This same rejection region is most powerful for every fixed \(\theta>0\), because for every \(\theta>0\) the likelihood ratio is increasing in \(Y\). Hence the test is uniformly most powerful for \(H_0:\theta=0\) versus \(H_a:\theta>0\).

Therefore the UMP level \(\alpha\) test is

\[
\boxed{\text{Reject } H_0 \text{ if } Y>1-\alpha.}
\]

Its size is exactly

\[
P_0(Y>1-\alpha)=\alpha.
\]

---

## (2) Power function

For general \(\theta>-1\), the CDF of \(Y\) is

\[
F_\theta(y)=P_\theta(Y\le y)
=\int_0^y (\theta+1)t^\theta\,dt
= y^{\theta+1},\qquad 0<y<1.
\]

Therefore the power function of the UMP test is

\[
\pi(\theta)
= P_\theta(Y>1-\alpha).
\]

Using the CDF,

\[
\pi(\theta)
=1-F_\theta(1-\alpha)
=1-(1-\alpha)^{\theta+1}.
\]

Thus

\[
\boxed{\pi(\theta)=1-(1-\alpha)^{\theta+1}.}
\]

In particular, at the null value,

\[
\pi(0)=1-(1-\alpha)=\alpha,
\]

so the test has exact level \(\alpha\).
